## Design

### 2026-10-07: # Started the Project

**1.6h**

# Started the Project

Got initial idea to try and open a curtain. So started researching parts to use and how to make a PCB.

Also looked at other designs to see if this was feasible. Looked at different designs, including ones that manually push the curtain along:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/565a00b5ac5c878b1bd4327c88d3d3ff19cc7ec4341a38dc36dee06dcd7172f2.png)

Which I actually really liked the look of, as they are a much better all round solution.

But as my curtains have a pull cord, I decided that it would be easier to make something for that (especially as it was my first PCB project (but mainly that I wouldn't be able to really fix it if it didn't work, as I'm not easily able to get parts remade after ordering)):

![Curtain Cord](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/b9e76ac33a13bcc3d189d1a359a76fe1a99bebb0fcd8e8a03cf97bfac29af19e.png)

### 2026-10-07: # Did the bulk of the Schematic work

**3.78h**

# Did the bulk of the Schematic work

Finally finished researching components, and started laying things out in easyEDA.
Now at a stage I am happy with, but still have to add a few more components.

Hoping that from this point on its gets a bit easier, as so far its been pretty complicated. Although I spent way too long trying to figure out how to use pin headers, and it turns out you don't even need them lol (at least in the schematic).

![PCB Schematic v1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/8d57acc4a0f5deee26658b55fcc6f958cbc1f2d7fc239c19368e5942ffccbe44.png)

Also did the complicated task of wiring up a k7805-1000r3 buck regulator, as had fun reading through the datasheet (on my phone) figuring out what it needed.

Although did also some AI just to fact check if things worked. Though I did find and connect all the parts manually (As I'm a beginner, I figured this was better than flooding the slack with "does this work").

### 2026-10-08: # Simplifying the Schematic

**2.52h**

# Simplifying the Schematic

Spent this session researching the components more, and whether they would actually work together.

Found out that using mosfets to switch the charging off would be painful, so got rid of them.

Regarding this as a first PCB project, its going fairly well I think, but I'm still yet to actually get onto the PCB phase.

### 2026-10-11: # Routing PCB

**2.5h**

# Routing PCB

Finally started routing the PCB.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/8dba82f9980c679dac0117db781c8474dda3e7e4cd7f1a626de2244aad4687e2.png)

So I initially tried using the Autorouter for this, as I thought it would be a lot faster, but it ended up with like 5 vias.

But I also had to go through and figure out what a good width for the traces was, so I ended up with basically 0.8mm for anything that could need mildly high current - so basically the power system and the main power bus.

Then had to figure out which things like U1, U2, R1 everything connected to - in the end, I did what I should have done before, and went back into the schematic to change them all to understandable names.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/235ae3484459c5ea22862548fdad098cd6f9ba32e9d112898d682016bcf9dc15.png)

And as I read that vias are bad, I decided to hand wire it.

And it was probably a good decision, as I managed to get that down to a single via lol. So much for Autorouters being good.

Its really nice seeing it come together.

Unfortunately though, as I'm adding up the BOM, I'd be getting everything from Aliexpress - aside from the PCB, then just one switching regulator to step down to 5V from LCSC (k7805 1000r3). So I'm trying to replace that with something else, but annoyingly there isn't anything I can find easily at the price I want with the specs I want. so that's what I'll be working on next.

Also didn't realise that the TMC 2209 drivers have different pinouts on the modules. Had previously assumed they were all the same, but now have to fork out some more money for a bigtreetech clone one, as I cant be bothered to redo the schematic for a different clone.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/53a3a75d35c93267490985edc1a38c12b93f93aef2b969682353b6004992e945.png)

### 2026-10-11: # Finished the Project

**3.83h**

# Finished the Project
### Finished Choosing Parts
Finally finished choosing the parts that I wanted for the project. Especially as some parts weren't viable or economic

### Routed the PCB
As a beginner to PCB design, I thought it would be much harder, especially given the expected current pull of the board. But it was actually really easy to route, and after my first go, I had no DRC errors.

![EasyEDA DRC check](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/2ee2c2d729556b90083bd3a7d52b3a7aaa07faaaeaa98d3500b038a8a21fae5f.png)

Also was made a lot simpler in that I could just use copper pours for the Ground plane.

### Finished the BOM
Spent a fair bit of time on Aliexpress and JLCPCB looking at how much things will cost, and it all seems to add up quite nicely.

![aliexpress checkout window](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/416319bffc8aa409ae5618ccaecb064b7df773c79f7bcc7be9355fddc10d3f09.png)

![jlcpcb checkout window](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/375e00f3889d514fd2d9984a22e3cd4ff96f5eddaff14631f334f52c121f8fcb.png)

(Especially as it looks like the PCB will be free, as I got given some coupons from creating an account)

Now I think I'm ready to submit.
